Asobi 1.0 (build 1757) Oct 22, 2026

  • Fixed: reopening a review no longer removes its notes from Kitsu. A review of a Kitsu playlist that was ended and reopened came back as it was before the review, and its live notes then took every note made in it out of Kitsu. Asobi now changes or removes a Kitsu note only when its frame is changed in this sitting.
  • Reopen brings a review back as it was left: End Review and Step Away keep its notes, marks, shots and recordings, saved or not. Your own session file isn’t written until you save.
  • Record the Session checks first: a microphone macOS won’t share stops it with the way to fix it; Siri and Dictation off says there’ll be no transcript. A recording that hears nothing says so within seconds, and one silent channel of the microphone no longer means a silent file.
  • Recordings stay with their review, so Replay Last Session Recording works after Reopen.
  • Kitsu source paths written on Linux or Windows (/media/…, K:\…, \\server\…) are found on this Mac, and a sequence named by its frames’ shared name opens as its folder.
Earlier updates

1.0 (build 1752) Oct 22, 2026

  • The fastest Mac renders the source frames: when the room is on a shot’s source, any studio Mac in the review that reaches it can render the full-resolution frames clients see when stopped, not only the host’s. The host times each Mac and asks the fastest; one that doesn’t answer in 3 seconds is passed over. The host can now push a shot it can’t reach itself.
  • Fixed: someone joining after a Flip for Everyone wasn’t told the room was on the source (a browser’s frame wasn’t marked source; Asobi Review kept the QuickTime).
  • Fixed: a Mac not in front was slowed by App Nap while delivering frames for the room.

1.0 (build 1747) Oct 22, 2026

  • Flip for Everyone (Playback ▸ Source, ⇧⌥⌘F) puts the whole room on a shot’s source in any review, clients included; again puts everyone back on the QuickTime. Flip All for Everyone does every shot with a source. ⌥⌘F stays your own.
  • Clients see the source: in a browser or Asobi Review, stopped on a frame of a flipped shot, they get that frame from the source at full resolution, through the display transform, marked SOURCE. Playing shows the QuickTime.

1.0 (build 1742) Oct 22, 2026

  • Internal reviews: Review ▸ Internal Review, while hosting, says everyone in the review is from the studio. A flip to source (⌥⌘F or Flip All) on any Asobi seat then shows for the whole room, sources are shared even with a passphrase, latecomers land on what the room shows, and every seat sees INTERNAL beside LIVE.
  • Browsers in an internal review parked on a frame of a clip the room shows on its source get that frame from the source at full resolution, through the display transform, marked “full frame · source”.
  • Flipping in any shared review now changes only the picture, for the host too, so the clip keeps its place for everyone.
  • Fixed: a clip shown on its source in a review was saved (and kept in the crash-recovery copy) with the source’s input space, so the QuickTime reopened decoded as the EXR.

1.0 (build 1737) Oct 22, 2026

  • Guests flip to source in a review without a passphrase. The host sends where each clip’s source is, and a guest’s Flip to Source Media (⌥⌘F) or Flip All shows it on their own screen only, with a SOURCE badge; the room keeps the review copy. A review with a passphrase sends no paths.
  • Paste a review link (⌘V) into an empty window to join, or drag one in from a browser or a message.
  • Show Original Frame (⌥R) on a review copy now says it is the review copy the host shared, not that it is the original.

1.0 (build 1734) Oct 21, 2026

  • Showcase viewing shows how each viewer’s connection did: its speed against what the piece needs, how long the picture took to come up and the piece to start, and any stops to load. Per visit, summed up above the visits, and in the CSV.
  • Conform reports list a shot’s plates as its source when its clips came from outside the cut (a color ref, an email), and no longer count the cut’s stand-in for it as missing. A new section, Plates from outside the cut, lists them with where their ranges came from.
  • Finding media no longer takes a file whose name merely starts with the same eight letters for the one the cut names.

1.0 (build 1728) Oct 20, 2026

  • Recording a session no longer turns the call and the clip audio down on your Mac while it records.

1.0 (build 1724) Oct 19, 2026

  • Update from Kitsu Playlist. Media menu, or the circling arrows at the top of the Playlist: late shots and new versions from the same Kitsu playlist come into a running review, and go out to everyone in it, on the web and in Asobi.
  • Export Compare with Edit Ref. Media ▸ Conformed Cut: the conform beside its Edit Ref as one QuickTime, lined up as Compare Edit Ref shows it.
  • Conform reports show a picture for every stacked layer (PL02, PL03).
  • Plate review movies are always 16:9, a plate of another shape kept whole inside it, so Kitsu shows it unstretched.
  • A pull of many plates makes each review movie and proxy from its own plate, never another one in the same folder.
  • Studio-made shots get their own card, and a shot in the cut with no footage gets its placeholder, pulled or not.
  • A re-cut keeps a shot’s name when its file isn’t on this Mac.
